ALPHABET CENTER · LETTER R

Letter R — Rabbit.

An orange rabbit hops in for the letter R. R growls like a friendly tiger — rrr — and the rabbit gives the growl two long ears to listen with.

Meet the letter, hear its sound, trace it together — then play. Everything on this page is free, gentle and paced for you.

THE LETTER SOUND

What does R say?

“r — rrr, a growling sound”

R says rrr — a growly sound made with a bouncy tongue. Pretend to be a tiger, then shrink it down: rrrabbit. The growl is the game.

TRACE THE LETTER

Trace R r together.

Follow the numbers with a finger — on screen or on each other’s palms. The arrows show the way to go, the numbers show where to start, and a grown-up reads the little script below each card. Slow and wobbly is exactly right.

Trace the uppercase R

Start at 1 at the top, pull straight down. Lift. Start at 2 at the top, curve out to the right, round the small bump and back to the stem. Lift. Start at 3 at the bump, slide down to the bottom right corner.

Trace the lowercase r

Start at 1, pull straight down. Lift. Start at 2 on the stem, curve up and over to the right.

TAKE IT OFF SCREEN

Rabbit hop.

Two minutes is plenty. Follow your child’s lead and stop while it is still fun — that is the whole method.

  1. 01

    Hop three times across the room, growling softly: rrr, rrr, rabbit!

  2. 02

    Nibble an imaginary carrot with fast little bites.

  3. 03

    Freeze like a still rabbit when you hear rrr — then hop to the sofa.

PLAY & PRACTICE

Games that use this letter.

The games mix every letter — play them after meeting two or three letters, or any day your child asks. No scores, no timers, no wrong answers that count.
